newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ BOWLERS SKITTLE SRI LANKA TO TIE SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ BOWLERS SKITTLE SRI LANKA TO TIE SERIES.

text.p: New Zealand's bowlers staged a courageous fightback to win Thursday's one-day cricket international against Sri Lanka and square the series.
Heath Davis captured four for 35 as the home side successfully defended a modest total of 201 by dismissing the world one-day champions for 132 in just 37.2 overs.
New Zealand's victory by 69 runs enabled them to tie the series, reduced to two matches after the first game was abandoned because of rain.
Davis recorded his best one-day international figures and received excellent support from Gavin Larsen and Nathan Astle.

Medium pacer Astle came on in the latter stages to take three for nine from six overs and Larsen stemmed the early flood of runs when he delivered four successive maidens to finish with none for nine off seven overs.

The match was tinged with controversy when Wellington umpire Evan Watkin gave Sri Lankan batsman Aravinda de Silva out, apparently for obstructing the field, before changing his mind and allowing de Silva to stay.
At the time de Silva was on 15 and Sri Lanka were 78 for three in the 17th over when de Silva played the ball back to the bowler Larsen.
Larsen retrieved the ball and attempted to throw down the stumps.
De Silva, standing between the bowler and the stumps, tried to hit the ball away with his bat, but it deflected off his pads, and he and captain Arjuna Ranatunga scrambled through for a single.
Watkin raised his finger after a brief delay but then overturned his initial decision, but it ultimately had no bearing on the outcome of the match as de Silva departed for 36 in the 36th over.
The New Zealand innings never got out of second gear after left arm seamers Chaminda Vaas and Nuwan Zoysa utilised the early seam and swing movement on offer.
The home side were reduced to 28 for three before Chris Cairns struck a hard-hit 56 from 79 balls, including seven boundaries, to raise hopes of a substantial score.
Vaas was in superb form, enjoying his best day of the tour as he picked up four for 26.
